title: What Happens Inside Your Face When You Blush?
description:
Embarrassment can redirect visible blood flow before you can stop it.

Facial blood vessels dilate and more blood becomes visible near the skin surface.

Blushing involves autonomic nervous-system responses and is concentrated in highly visible facial, ear, neck and upper-chest vasculature.

A blush often becomes visible seconds after the emotional trigger, even though the reaction is involuntary.
